summary.oneLiner: RateGain is the dominant B2B SaaS platform for hotel and airline distribution in India, with expanding global footprint and AI-powered revenue management tools driving margin expansion. Strong corporate travel recovery and new enterprise contracts are accelerating top-line growth.

one-line thesis: RateGain is the dominant B2B SaaS platform for hotel and airline distribution in India, with expanding global footprint and AI-powered revenue management tools driving margin expansion. Strong corporate travel recovery and new enterprise contracts are accelerating top-line growth.
financial scorecard: rev:+22% YoY; EBITDA:+31% YoY; PAT:+45% YoY; orderbook:₹1,200 Cr; netdebt:₹-85 Cr (net cash)
guidance: FY27 revenue guidance of ₹2,100–2,200 Cr (25–30% YoY growth); EBITDA margin target of 28–30%; EBITDA growth to outpace revenue growth due to operating leverage
order book & pipeline: ₹1,200 Cr (up 40% YoY), including ₹450 Cr from new enterprise contracts with European hotel chains and ₹300 Cr from airline connectivity upgrades
segment / subsidiary detail: Hotel distribution: 52% of rev (up 18% YoY); Airline connectivity: 20% (up 35% YoY); Revenue management: 15% (up 50% YoY); Corporate travel: 8% (up 65% YoY); Data analytics: 5% (up 70% YoY)
growth verticals / optionality: Expansion into Southeast Asia (Singapore, Thailand); white-label SaaS for mid-tier hotel chains; AI-powered demand forecasting licensing to non-travel sectors (events, hospitality)
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin: 82% (up 300 bps YoY); EBITDA margin: 26.5% (up 350 bps YoY); cost savings from AI automation in customer support (-18% OpEx per ticket); cloud infrastructure optimization reduced AWS spend by 12%
capex / expansion: ₹42 Cr in FY26 (primarily AI model training, cloud infrastructure, R&D); FY27 capex guidance: ₹55–60 Cr (mainly for global data centers and AI product suite)
capital allocation: Prioritizing R&D (45% of free cash flow); share buybacks (₹100 Cr announced in Q4); strategic M&A in EU/US travel tech (targeting niche revenue management startups); no dividend payout
risks & watch-items: Regulatory scrutiny on OTA commission structures in EU; currency volatility in USD/EUR revenue; dependency on third-party API providers (Amadeus, Sabre); talent attrition in AI engineering team
management quality / tone: Highly confident; emphasized 'unprecedented demand' for AI-driven pricing tools; called corporate travel recovery 'structural, not cyclical'; expressed urgency to capture global market share before Chinese competitors expand
non-obvious takeaways: RateGain's proprietary 'demand elasticity engine' is being piloted by 3 European airport authorities for non-airline retail pricing — potential $50M TAM expansion beyond travel tech

themes.title: Hospitality & travel up-cycle
themes.need: Q1FY27 split hotels from airlines. INDHOTEL delivered a 17th consecutive record quarter - consolidated revenue INR 2,419cr (+15%), EBITDA INR 753cr at 31.1%, standalone occupancy jumping to 82% from 76% on a 41.8% standalone EBITDA margin, and asset-light management-fee income INR 168cr (+26%) - with management now framing the West-Asia war as a NET tailwind because outbound travel stays home; leisure RevPAR (Rajasthan/Goa) ran up high-20s. Airlines got the mirror image: INDIGO's EBITDAR margin collapsed from 28.0% to 15.6% on blended ATF of ~INR 140-150/litre versus INR 85-90 pre-war (fuel CASK +~80% YoY), leaving yield as the only defence. MHRIL shows domestic leisure premiumisation is real - Keystone average unit realisation +73% to INR 14.4 lakh on stable gross sales. LEMONTREE/CHALET/SAMHI/THELEELA ride the same occupancy-led room cycle; TRAVELFOOD/TBOTEK/DREAMFOLKS remain levered to airport PAX and B2B travel.
themes.driver: Occupancy-led (not rate-led) RevPAR compounding plus INDHOTEL's Ginger conversion cadence stepping 15->20->25->40 per quarter through FY27; for airlines the swing is INDIGO's guided Q2 PRASK growth of 'more than 25%' on flattish capacity against ATF cracks.

themes.title: Digital platforms, SaaS, payments & cybersecurity
themes.need: Digital-public-infrastructure scale, enterprise SaaS and a compliance/security upcycle drive a distinct platform cohort. PINELABS/NPST/CMSINFO on payments; AURIONPRO/NEWGEN/NUCLEUS/ROUTE/TANLA on banking/CPaaS software; EMUDHRA/META(544441)/AURIONPRO on digital-identity & cybersecurity; CAPILLARY/MAPMYINDIA/NAZARA on SaaS/geospatial/gaming. Q1FY27 anchored the payments leg: PAYTM's GMV grew 31% YoY (accelerating 23% -> 27% -> 31%) with merchant payments about 80% of the financial-services mix and 25-30 lakh device additions a year on a distribution-only lending model (no book, no FLDG); MOBIKWIK posted payments GMV of INR 52,400cr (+58% YoY), a 13th consecutive record quarter and India's largest wallet by GTV at ~20% share, against only ~INR 3,200cr of digital-credit GMV. OFSS adds the banking-software annuity, with RPO +17% YoY versus revenue +7% and licence-and-cloud revenue +13% at a 44% operating margin.
themes.driver: Deal/ARR additions; festive digital-payments TPV; merchant-device additions; RBI/regulatory compliance-driven security spend.
